name: Scape Goat The
overview: The scapegoat, chosen by lot from two goats presented before the Lord, was a vital part of the sin offering on the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:5-8). Aaron, the high priest, laid both hands upon the live goat's head, confessing all the iniquities and transgressions of Israel, thereby transferring their sins onto the goat (Leviticus 16:21). This goat was then sent away by the hand of a fit man into an uninhabited wilderness, symbolically carrying away the people's sins and making atonement for them (Leviticus 16:22). This ritual prefigures Christ, who bore the sins of His people and was sent away to bring true cleansing and reconciliation with God.
